title: TS SDK: transformable frames + consumer-takeover interop for AsyncIterator <-> WebStream
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Add a new consumer-takeover pattern and 'FrameTransformer' primitive for the TypeScript SDK to make AsyncIterator and Web Stream interoperable while preserving typed frame boundaries, backpressure signals, and resume/retry semantics. This ticket covers design, implementation, tests, examples, and a staged rollout. Goal: make it ergonomically easy for client code to switch between for-await-of and ReadableStream consumers without losing semantics or causing silent token duplication/loss.
acceptance_criteria: 1) SDK exposes a FrameTransformer<T> that can sit between any AsyncIterable<T> and ReadableStream<T> without buffering unlimited items. 2) Switching consumer mode mid-flight (for-await-of -> stream.getReader()) transfers ownership cleanly and respects outstanding abort signals. 3) Backpressure/pausing from a downstream reader is honored by the SDK runtime and reflected in kernel batching hints. 4) Clear integration examples (3) published in /examples/ts-streaming with test harnesses to validate no-duplicate/no-drop at 10k concurrent short-lived streams. 5) Docs and migration guide merged and internal samples updated.
notes: 2025-10-22: Kickoff — synced with DX and runtime teams. Initial constraints: must not add native Node-only APIs (must work in Deno/browser).

2025-10-24: Prototype complete — implemented lightweight FrameTransformer that attaches a small sequence-id header to frames to preserve ordering across consumer swaps. Prototype uses single-slot buffer to enable takeover without full draining.

2025-10-27: Design decision — dropped using MessageChannel for takeover due to Edge and Safari compatibility; opted for Promise-based handoff with AbortController signals. Trade-off: slightly more complex state machine but better cross-platform behavior.
2025-10-29: PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-ts/pull/4822 — includes transformer, utils, and basic tests. Needs review from infra/runtime (Nina) for kernel hinting integration.

2025-10-30: Found edge case — when consumer A partially reads a chunk and then relinquishes, previous approach could duplicate token segments. Fix: include chunk-offset metadata in frame header and ensure atomic commit on consumer confirmation.

2025-11-01: Performance run: single GPU runtime with 96 concurrent streams at 2KB average frame size — overhead ~3.4% measured on per-token latency vs baseline streaming shim. Acceptable for default on/off flag.

2025-11-01: Next: write ergonomic examples (for-await-of -> stream reader takeover; stream -> for-await-of fallback; cancellation on takeover), full fuzz tests for reordering/duplicates, and docs PR for SDK website. Schedule staged rollout behind feature flag.

Followups: add TypeScript types for Frame<T>, publish migration guide for existing users who rely on raw byte streams. Consider a future runtime hint API to convert consumer backpressure into batching window size adjustments.
implementation_notes: Key primitives: FrameTransformer<T>, takeover(): Promise<void>, drainUntilCommit(), commitFrame(seq), frameHeaders include {seq, offset, id}. Provide two high-level helpers: asReadableStream(asyncIterable, opts) and asAsyncIterable(readableStream, opts). Expose feature flag 'streamInterop.takeoverV1' default false until rollout. Ensure Node/Deno/browser bundling via conditional exports. Keep polyfills out of prod bundle; provide separate package '@redwood/sdk-stream-utils' for helpers.
test_plan: Unit tests for transformer state machine (edge transitions), integration tests with real SDK runtime through a local mock runtime that simulates throttling and partial chunking, fuzz tests to inject reorder/duplicate/drop with property checks, end-to-end perf smoke that compares P95 token latency with baseline. Add CI job 'ts-streaming-interop' that runs across node16,node20,deno and a headless-chrome runner for ReadableStream semantics.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge behind feature flag. 2) Canary enabled for 10% of SDK users via environment flag in hosted. 3) Monitor errors and duplicate/dropped frames (log metric: sdk.stream.takeover.errors). 4) Expand to 50% after 72h stable. 5) Default-on in next minor (ts-sdk-2026.02) with migration docs.
